reference: GNU coreutils chown invoked by system Bash is the independent oracle for runnable parity cases. The runner provides a deterministic runner user/group whose IDs own each private fixture. GNU ln is used only to construct a dangling symlink for the -h and dereference cases; the behavior under test is chown.
coverage: Numeric owner and named owner/group resolution for the fixture's existing identity
-h changes a dangling symlink itself; default behavior follows it
Invalid owner, negative numeric owner, missing operand, status, diagnostics, and unchanged fixture effects
exclusions: A successful ownership change to a distinct UID or non-member GID needs CAP_CHOWN or a reviewed syscall mock. The mandatory runner has no capabilities, so that operation is deferred rather than represented as passing.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify the registered chown loadable as a builtin; this is availability metadata, not operation coverage.
Bash help must recognize the documented chown loadable entry. The fixture emits a marker after help succeeds so documentation wording is not mistaken for GNU parity.
A numeric owner equal to the fixture's effective UID and named group runner exercise numeric owner parsing and OWNER:GROUP with a safe identity-preserving request.
cases.script:
printf 'owned fixture\n' > item
chown "$EUID:runner" item
/usr/bin/stat -c "%u:%g %a" item

cases.purpose: The :GROUP form must leave owner unchanged and accept multiple relative file operands; runner is the file's existing primary group.
cases.script:
printf 'first\n' > first
printf 'second\n' > second
chown :runner first second
/usr/bin/stat -c "%u:%g %a" first second

cases.purpose: GNU accepts the legacy OWNER.GROUP spelling but emits a deprecation warning. Compare that diagnostic policy as well as status and effects; the loadable source has a legacy dot parser.
cases.script:
printf 'legacy syntax\n' > item
chown runner.runner item
/usr/bin/stat -c "%u:%g %a" item

cases.purpose: With -h, chown must operate on a dangling symlink itself; without no-follow behavior this same path would fail because its target does not exist.
cases.script:
ln -s missing-target link
chown -h runner:runner link
/usr/bin/stat -c "%u:%g %a" link

cases.purpose: Without -h, chown follows a dangling symlink and reports the missing target; capture the command failure before reporting its status.
cases.script:
ln -s missing-target link
rc=0
chown runner:runner link || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: An unresolvable nonnumeric owner must fail with a diagnostic and leave the private file unchanged.
cases.script:
printf 'unchanged\n' > item
rc=0
chown no_such_user_bashos_suite_987654 item || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: GNU chown does not accept a negative UID as a valid owner. This also checks that -1 is not accidentally treated as the chown(2) unchanged-UID sentinel by the command parser.
cases.script:
printf 'unchanged\n' > item
rc=0
chown -- -1 item || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: A missing later operand must produce a failure status and diagnostic after a valid operand; capture the aggregate command status.
cases.script:
printf 'fixture\n' > present
rc=0
chown :runner present missing || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.script:

chown "$EUID" item
chown :runner item
chown "$EUID:$(/usr/bin/id -g)" item
